Michael Olise to miss Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga game vs. Hamburg

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (207 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has confirmed that they will be without Michael Olise for their Bundesliga game against Hamburg on Saturday.
  • The Frenchman was injured in last weekend’s 1-1 draw against Cologne and subsequently missed Bayern’s UEFA Champions League defeat against Lille on Wednesday night.
  • He is, though, ruled out of Bayern’s game this weekend.

Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has confirmed that they will be without Michael Olise for their Bundesliga game against Hamburg on Saturday.

The Frenchman was injured in last weekend’s 1-1 draw against Cologne and subsequently missed Bayern’s UEFA Champions League defeat against Lille on Wednesday night. Olise, who left the Allianz Arena on crutches after a challenge from Cologne’s Tom Krauß at the edge of the box, has been wearing a VACOped brace to help with the recovery process after suffering bruising on his left foot.

He is, though, ruled out of Bayern’s game this weekend. “Olise won’t be there,” Kompany stated at Friday’s press conference. While Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari and Harry Kane are all sidelined, Luis Díaz returned against Lille – in a game where Lennart Karl led the attack – after sustaining a thigh injury during their 2-2 draw against Arsenal in October.

It has been revealed that an attacking trio of Konrad Laimer, Tom Bischof and Nathaniel Brown started on Wednesday, but Kompany remained tight-lipped on who will start against HSV. “We have to make the most of the hand we’ve been dealt,” he added. “So everything remains open, but our expectations and standards remain exactly the same.”.

Tech Report: Maresca in conferenza stampa: “Il Napoli si è difeso bene e ha concretizzato due occasioni”

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (490 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Iamnaples

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo il pareggio in Champions League contro il Napoli.:  “Noi cerchiamo sempre di vincere, ma se non puoi vincere è importante non perdere.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

Recent findings suggest that enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo il pareggio in Champions League contro il Napoli.:  “Noi cerchiamo sempre di vincere, ma se non puoi vincere è importante non perdere. Prendiamo il punto, ne abbiamo 10 in classifica e in fin dei conti è un buon risultato per andare avanti. Ricordo un loro calcio d’angolo e i due gol, in questo momento gli avversari sono cinici davanti alla porta. C’è poco da fare, accettiamo il punto e andiamo avanti. L’impatto sui giocatori? In questo momento va un po’ così, le prime dieci partite siamo stati sempre noi a sbloccare, mentre ora sono gli avversari a farlo. Non credo che abbia un impatto sulla fiducia dei calciatori, devi correre un po’ di più se sei in svantaggio, ma abbiamo lottato fino alla fine e serve alzare l’asticella. Non dobbiamo subire questi gol, basta vedere le statistiche a nostro favore. C’è uno squilibrio tra le occasioni create e i gol segnati. Anche Cherki ha detto che mancava energia? Siamo stati molto aggressivi. I due terzini in posizione centrale? Abbiamo iniziato con Bouaddi e Enzo in mezzo per vedere se potevamo trovare equilibrio, poi Nico e Matheus Nunes hanno fatto bene, è un’altra opzione per noi. Volevamo fare qualche cambio ed essere più fisici in mezzo al campo per contrastarli. La qualità del gol di Cherki? Ottimo, sono contento per lui. Ha fatto bene, sappiamo che sa giocare meglio centralmente, ma sta facendo bene. Ci aspettavamo un Napoli col blocco basso, era difficile trovare soluzioni, ma dovevamo evitare di concedere i gol concessi, erano evitabili. I cori a Donnarumma? Non ci ho fatto caso, ero concentrato sulla partita. Era difficile attaccare il Napoli, erano in undici sulla linea dell’area. Potevamo fare meglio nelle chance avute e cercare di evitare le due occasioni concesse. Hanno avuto quelle e il corner di Beukema, c’è rammarico per non aver vinto, ma se non puoi farlo è importante anche non perdere. Non vinciamo da tre partite, ma i meriti del Napoli sono importanti: si è difeso bene e ha concretizzato due occasioni. Noi potevamo fare meglio, il Napoli ha avuto i suoi meriti e ha fatto una buona gara”.

#222023. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

📅 25 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4152 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4152 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
  • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
  • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his upcoming club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke mentioned: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

According to recent reports, newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

In a recent development, glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He stated: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

It has been revealed that the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

It has been revealed that ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a latest forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

According to recent reports, speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon mentioned: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

Recent findings suggest that of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

Aug 29: Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestSep 5: Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham HotspurSep 12: Aston Villa vs Nottingham ForestSep 19: Nottingham Forest vs CoventryOct 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest.

A tough night for the home teams...

Cardiff City 1 Norwich 2Doncaster Rovers 1 Middlesbrough 3Barnsley 3 Crewe Alexandra 2Blackburn Rovers 1 Sheffield United 2Blackpool 1 Lincoln City 4Cambridge United 0 Millwall 1Fleetwood Town 4 Shrewsbury Town 0Ipswich Town 3 Leicester City 1Plymouth 2 Coventry City 4Sheffield Wednesday 0 Wolverhampton Wanderers 2Southampton 1 West Ham United 4Stevenage Town 0 Reading 3Stoke City 1 Hull City 1 (4-5 pens)Walsall 0 Leyton Orient 0 (5-6 pens)Watford 1 Peterborough United 5Birmingham City 1 Brentford 6Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2.

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

Recent findings suggest that there is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

There will be six minutes of added time.

Industry observers note that that just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

According to recent reports, calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

Recent findings suggest that the “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu debuts a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

Sources indicate that it's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP.

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

Industry observers note that there’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

In a recent development, glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

It has been revealed that chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE.

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Sources indicate that both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

According to recent reports, should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

Leeds have only won four from 10.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ.

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

In a recent development, and, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Recent findings suggest that another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Sources indicate that ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Sources indicate that oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Industry observers note that elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

In a recent development, another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

In a recent development, nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

Sources indicate that the game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sources indicate that sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w.

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

In a recent development, both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

According to recent reports, chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

It has been revealed that leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James reveals off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

It has been revealed that aina rolls out a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Recent findings suggest that players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”.

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9.

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”.

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke stated: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”.

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a significant believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”.

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

🏆x4⃣ pic.twitter.com/DRPXFa2kM3.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood.

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi.

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha.

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin.

The massive breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

In a recent development, 📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi.

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

It has been revealed that our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj.

It has been revealed that welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s fresh head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

It has been revealed that establishing the Weserstadion as a fortress, Bremen have won four and drawn one of their home games – scoring 14 goals, while keeping successive clean sheets in their last two games. Their latest result at home being last weekend’s 4-0 thrashing on Hamburg in the Nordderby.

In total, Thioune – who recently signed a contract extension – has guided his team to five wins, three draws and two defeats from their opening ten games, which places Bremen in sixth. A win tonight will move the Grün-Weißen above Bayer Leverkusen.

Marco Grüll is sidelined with a calf injury, but could “possibly [return] even next week,” states Thioune, who also offered an update on Justin Njinmah: “At the moment, I’m very concerned and not convinced he’ll be able to support us. He did, though, leave the door open for a potential start.

With 10 goals in 10 Bundesliga games in 2026/27, Niclas Füllkrug will look to add to his tally against the Bundesliga’s joint-worst defence this season.

Karl Hein – Arthur, Amos Pieper, Marco Friedl, Olivier Deman – Ludovit Reis, Youri Regeer – Eren Dinkci, Chuki, Justin Njinmah – Niclas Füllkrug.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:08 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:56 EST, 23 November 2026.

Jack Grealish returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being made unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline, and came off the bench at half-time against Brentford on Monday.

The Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He had not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a 'breach of club discipline' and a lack of fitness thereafter.

He last featured on October 17, over a month ago, but returned to the match day squad to take on Brentford on Monday night – named on the substitutes' bench. He was introduced at half-time for Tyrique George, with the Toffees 2-0 down and down to 10 men after James Tarkowski's red card. They would ultimately lose 4-0.

Manager David Moyes said ahead of the game: 'He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

It has been revealed that 'We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don't want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn't be.'.

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: 'He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?'.

Jack Grealish (right) returned to Everton action on Monday for the first time since being punished for missing training.

He was named on the bench against Brentford, coming on for Tyrique George at half-time.

Everton had won their last three games and went into Monday's match sixth in the table. The result, though, was a blow as they dropped to ninth.

In a recent development, asked what Grealish can offer, Moyes added: 'Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

'But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

'I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.'.

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart emoji)'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the strength of Hoffenheim’s bench proved decisive in Thursday evening’s 3-1 Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz. Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club.

Hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him.

“No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.”.

Ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker.

Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench.

“Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.”.

According to recent reports, hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen, Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist.

Sources indicate that despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half.

Baumann acknowledged that Hoffenheim remain in a developmental phase. The German international nevertheless welcomed the response after halftime, which helped lift Ilzer’s side to 15th place in the Europa League standings.

Thursday’s comeback thus highlighted both the shortcomings Hoffenheim must address and the considerable resources Ilzer has at his disposal. With the likes of Wimmer, Kramaric, Conté, and Moerstedt capable of influencing matches from the bench, the TSG trainer certainly has options when his starting XI struggles to find its rhythm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest massive-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his fresh club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” noted De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

According to recent reports, “We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

Industry observers note that "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their fresh song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi remarked. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Industry observers note that buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi stated: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

Industry observers note that “Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against substantial teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a significant player for us.

Sources indicate that “I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”.

Recent findings suggest that omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most notable.”.

#222012. ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany

ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that werder Bremen is the best team in northern Germany.
  • Bremen did more than just win that game; they demonstrated their quality this season and their ability to maximise the potential of their players to become a highly efficient team.
  • Sources indicate that this is the issue: The underlying numbers, in this case expected goals (xG), indicate that the game was actually very close – not as one-sided as the result suggests.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that werder Bremen is the best team in northern Germany. At least that is what was evident from last weekend’s Nordderby, when they successfully beat Hamburg 4–0 at the Weserstadion.

Bremen did more than just win that game; they demonstrated their quality this season and their ability to maximise the potential of their players to become a highly efficient team.

Sources indicate that this is the issue: The underlying numbers, in this case expected goals (xG), indicate that the game was actually very close – not as one-sided as the result suggests. HSV even had 1.54 compared to Bremen’s 1.52 in front of xG, per Opta.

It has been revealed that so, being able to win by a four-goal margin despite losing on xG demonstrates just how effective Bremen are as a team. Get German Football News’ Bergas investigates why….

It has been revealed that yes, HSV has more numbers in front of xG. However, if we look at the xG data itself, 1.03 of HSV’s 1.54 came after they fell behind in the 55th minute. In this situation, the state of the game changed, with HSV adopting a more proactive approach with the ball.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, between minutes 1 and 54, when the score was still 0–0, HSV only achieved an xG of 0.5 (Bremen had 0.84). This is why xG is not the best metric with which to measure HSV’s performance in this game, because the state of the game forced them to create more chances in order to catch up, resulting in lots of shots. In fact, however, they weren’t really dangerous enough to challenge or harm Bremen.

Looking at other metrics such as key passes, HSV weren’t superior either during the even time when the score was still 0–0. In that period, they made four key passes compared to Bremen’s eight. HSV found it much harder to create shots than the home team. Even in the first half, when Bremen were underperforming in parts, HSV didn’t look particularly threatening.

Bremen flexible defensive structure made HSV toothless.

One of the reasons for that is Bremen’s flexibility in their approach to HSV when defending. In the first half, they often used a man-to-man approach (which was more aggressive), which successfully forced HSV to use long balls to progress the ball to the final third, particularly on their left side.

In a recent development, in this long-ball scenario, Bremen also had the advantage when it came to closing down HSV attacks. The problem for Bremen arose when HSV successfully won the second ball, creating a situation in which Amos Pieper had to defend one-on-one against the opponent.

Industry observers note that pieper struggled in the early stages of the game against HSV’s pacey attackers and received a yellow card in the first half, but played safely for the rest of the game and successfully avoided another red card. This was also thanks to Bremen’s improved defensive structure in the second half. They were not as aggressive as before, but rather kept their double six close to their defensive line. With this defensive structure, HSV were unable to find the free space in front of Bremen’s defensive line that they had exploited in the first half.

Recent findings suggest that even if HSV were able to progress, Bremen’s man-to-man marking prevented them from being exploited by HSV’s overload, which they usually created through asymmetrical or free movement by their players. With every player having their own marker, that situation was difficult to create.

Directness and quality help Bremen win the game.

Sources indicate that one noticeable development from Werder Bremen this season is their flexibility with the ball. Bremen can be a team that dominates possession, but they can also be very dangerous when they need to play directly. This Nordderby is a perfect example of that.

In the minute before their second goal, Bremen only made two passes. Before the fourth goal? Only three. They can score with short sequences because they are very effective. The Bremen players really know how to make direct passes forward and progressive runs to enter the final third as quickly as possible. They don’t like to slow things down unnecessarily.

This behaviour is exemplified by players such as Justin Njinmah, Marco Grüll, Eren Dinkçi, Mitchell Weiser and Niclas Füllkrug, who excel in direct situations. Füllkrug is special because he knows many ways to score a goal, which has made Bremen more effective this season.

Bremen fans will be hoping that this form is sustainable for the rest of the season. While they have been flexible in terms of their attacking style and have been able to be efficient thanks to the quality of their players, at some point this season they may need a consistent pattern of attacks to help them create big chances.

In a recent development, it is clear from this game that HSV need their attackers to show more initiative in the final third. Of all the starters, only Albert Grønbæk consistently tries to create chances in the final third. He made some dribbles to try to break Bremen’s defensive structure and attempted some passes. However, one player is not enough.

Fabio Vieira came on in the second half, but it was too late to help HSV elevate their game. This was made worse by the fact that their top scorer, Miro Muheim, was injured early in the first half. Without their top creators and scorers, HSV practically didn’t have any much ideas in the game.

This problem is not upcoming. Spectacular goals from outside the box in previous games may have obscured this. However, to survive from game to game, HSV needs more than that. They need a consistent and sustainable initiative in the final third to help them create chances, as well as more initiative from their players to take risks and do more than just shoot from outside the box.

GGFN | Bergas – reporting from the Weserstadion.

La vittoria contro lo Stoccarda è stata importante per l'Inter non soltanto dal punto di vista sportivo, ma anche sotto il profilo economico. Il 2-0 firmato da Sucic e Lautaro Martinez ha garantito alla società nerazzurra altri 2,1 milioni di euro di premi UEFA.

L'Inter occupa il nono posto con 62,8 milioni di euro già garantiti, rispetto ai 60,7 milioni precedenti alla sfida con i tedeschi.

I nerazzurri sono l'unica squadra italiana presente nella top 10, a soli 500mila euro dal Borussia Dortmund e a un milione dal Barcellona. Alle spalle della società di viale della Liberazione c'è invece il Manchester United, fermo a 58,4 milioni.

In testa alla graduatoria figura il Paris Saint-Germain con 76,2 milioni, seguito dal Real Madrid con 75,1 e dal Liverpool con 72,8.

L'Inter ha dunque ancora la possibilità di incrementare sensibilmente il proprio bottino nelle ultime tre giornate della fase campionato, sia attraverso i premi per i risultati delle singole partite sia attraverso quelli legati al piazzamento finale e all'eventuale qualificazione alla fase a eliminazione diretta.

I 62,8 milioni rappresentano quindi la cifra minima già assicurata ai nerazzurri, senza considerare gli incassi al botteghino e gli ulteriori introiti commerciali legati alla partecipazione alla Champions League.

Freiburg’s Christian Günter demands tougher punishment after another incident of penalty-spot sabotage

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that SC Freiburg captain Christian Günter has called for harsher punishment for players who deliberately interfere with the penalty spot following a controversial incident during Thursday evening’s 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente.
  • Industry observers note that four players subsequently received yellow cards, but Vennegoor of Hesselink escaped a booking.
  • It has been revealed that “I would go so far as to say, as a referee, that he deserves a straight red card,” Günter – as quoted by Kicker – remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that SC Freiburg captain Christian Günter has called for harsher punishment for players who deliberately interfere with the penalty spot following a controversial incident during Thursday evening’s 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente. Freiburg were awarded a late penalty after substitute Derry Scherhant drew a foul from Bart van Rooij in the 89th minute. Before Matthias Ginter could take the spot kick, Twente striker Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink attempted to tear up the penalty spot with his spikes, provoking a confrontation involving several players from both sides.

Industry observers note that four players subsequently received yellow cards, but Vennegoor of Hesselink escaped a booking. Speaking after the match, Günter condemned the Dutch striker’s actions as “extreme unsporting behaviour” and suggested that such incidents warrant a straight red card. The Freiburg captain argued that football’s lawmakers should consider introducing stricter disciplinary provisions to prevent similar incidents.

It has been revealed that “I would go so far as to say, as a referee, that he deserves a straight red card,” Günter – as quoted by Kicker – remarked. “Do that once, and nobody will go near the penalty spot again.”.

The incident was not an isolated case of players attempting to interfere with penalty takers. During France’s 1-0 World Cup victory over Paraguay in July, defender Gustavo Velázquez attempted to damage the penalty spot before Kylian Mbappé converted the decisive spot kick.

Recent findings suggest that A similar controversy arose in September when Mainz midfielder Nadiem Amiri dragged his studs across the penalty spot before Kevin Diks attempted a penalty for Borussia Mönchengladbach. Diks subsequently struck the post in a match Mainz won 4-3. Amiri escaped punishment, prompting former German international Dietmar Hamann to demand a suspension for the midfielder.

In a recent development, under IFAB Law 12, making unauthorized markings on the pitch is a cautionable offence. Deliberately damaging the penalty spot does not, however, automatically warrant a dismissal. Günter’s proposed rule change would therefore introduce considerably harsher punishment for conduct that has already caused controversy at both international and Bundesliga level.

Scherhant, who won the penalty, appeared less interested in pursuing the controversy after the final whistle.

“Yeah, the opponent tried to sabotage the penalty spot and after that there was some hustle and bustle,” Scherhant remarked in the mixed zone afterwards. “That it gets to that point, that’s naturally not so cool, but I don’t think we need to keep talking about it. We got the points in a game that was difficult for us.”.

Sources indicate that the ensuing penalty nevertheless produced further drama. Ginter struck the right post with his attempt but reacted promptly enough to avoid touching the rebound. Scherhant kept the move alive, Yannik Engelhardt subsequently attempted a backheel, and Niklas Beste eventually converted from close range.

It has been revealed that günter praised Ginter’s awareness in avoiding an illegal second touch and considered Freiburg’s eventual winner a fitting outcome after the preceding controversy. The dramatic conclusion enabled Freiburg to extend their winning streak to six competitive matches and maintain their remarkable run of 14 consecutive European home victories, a streak that began under Christian Streich with a 5-0 Europa League victory over Serbian outfit TSC Bačka Topola on November 9, 2023.

Breaking: IT'S A GAME CHANGER! Scotland to co-host Women's World Cup with England, Northern Ireland and Wales in 2035

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:05 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Scotland, England, Northern Ireland and Wales have been confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 Women’s World Cup.
  • The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:05 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 23 November 2026.

Scotland, England, Northern Ireland and Wales have been confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

It will be the first men’s or women’s World Cup finals to be staged in the UK since the 1966 men’s tournament was held in England.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland (Hampden and Easter Road) and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams.

A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea stadium – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 stadiums across the four nations.

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold.

Joy for Spain after they defeated England in the 2023 Women's World Cup final.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir says the World Cup will take the nation's game to another level.

FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

For England this represents another chance to host a major women’s tournament, having hosted the European Championship in 2022 which the Lionesses won.

The Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: 'The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

'Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep – and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.'.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino announces the home nations as World Cup hosts.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir added: 'The women’s game in Scotland has so much potential and this tournament is a real opportunity to drive momentum and help take it to another level both nationally and internationally.

'We’re so proud to play our part in welcoming the world in 2035 and I know I speak on behalf of all of the players and staff when I say that we are ready to rise to the challenge and help deliver a truly memorable, world-class tournament.'.

England forward Michelle Agyemang mentioned it was 'incredibly special' and added: 'I’ve been lucky enough to know what it feels like to play for my country in a major tournament, and those are moments you dream about as a young girl playing football.

Industry observers note that 'The thought of another generation growing up knowing that the biggest stage in the game is coming to their home country is amazing. To have the chance to play in a home World Cup would be a dream, but even more exciting is thinking about all the girls watching who might see 2035 and believe they can be part of it one day.'.

SFA chief Ian Maxwell states tournament will be 'most significant thing to happen to women's and girls' game in Scotland'.

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be 'the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland'.

He remarked: 'The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.'.

First Minister John Swinney stated: 'This is fantastic news for Scotland. We have proved time and again that we are a world-class host, and I am delighted that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035 will be held in Scotland alongside England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

'The timing is ideal. Project 2035, our new long-term plan to grow the girls’ and women’s game, aims to establish Scotland as a leading nation for women’s football by 2035. Our newly established girls’ and women’s football taskforce will help to make this happen, capitalising on the World Cup and leaving a lasting legacy for communities across the country.

Recent findings suggest that 'Scotland is building a remarkable reputation for hosting major events, and the FIFA Women’s World Cup joins the Tour de France Grand Départ, The Open, the World Rally Championships and UEFA EURO 2028 in promising to showcase what our country has to offer. We will make sure each one of these amazing sporting events delivers for our economy, supporting jobs, businesses and tourism.'.

Freiburg in ecstasy as remarkable winning streak extends to six matches

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SC Freiburg head coach Julian Schuster has praised his squad’s extraordinary team spirit following Thursday evening’s dramatic 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente.
  • In a recent development, the Freiburg trainer made six changes to the starting XI that defeated Elversberg 1-0 in the Bundesliga last weekend.Cyriaque Irié rewarded Schuster’s faith by scoring the opener in the 11th minute, but Twente remained the more threatening side for much of the first half and eventually equalized through a Younes Taha free kick in the 62nd.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SC Freiburg head coach Julian Schuster has praised his squad’s extraordinary team spirit following Thursday evening’s dramatic 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente. The Breisgauer secured their sixth consecutive competitive victory thanks to a stoppage-time winner from Niklas Beste, with Schuster emphasizing the importance of a united dressing room in navigating a demanding schedule.

In a recent development, the Freiburg trainer made six changes to the starting XI that defeated Elversberg 1-0 in the Bundesliga last weekend.Cyriaque Irié rewarded Schuster’s faith by scoring the opener in the 11th minute, but Twente remained the more threatening side for much of the first half and eventually equalized through a Younes Taha free kick in the 62nd. Freiburg nevertheless found another way to win. Substitute Derry Scherhant earned a penalty in the 89th minute, and fellow replacement Beste eventually converted the loose ball after Matthias Ginter’s spot kick struck the post.

Industry observers note that speaking to a group of assembled journalists after the post-match press conference, Schuster drew attention to the collective celebrations following Beste’s dramatic winner. The 41-year-old suggested that the team’s togetherness gives him the confidence to rotate extensively without compromising Freiburg’s competitiveness.

It has been revealed that “That scene in which the team celebrated together is emblematic of this group,” Schuster told the journalists. “That lends us the strength to rotate the squad with full confidence. One sees this with various clubs that have to deal with extreme pressure during this phase [of the season]. There’s also players who have international obligations. The pressure is extreme.

“One really can’t leave anyone out,” Schuster continued. “We have this depth and there’s always little things that leave one needing to switch it up. Then it’s nice when players are ready to serve on a regular basis and not to get caught up in the competition of who makes the team sheet. That’s extremely crucial and I’m very pleased with the lads who started today and were able to make a contribution to the win.”.

It has been revealed that schuster’s observations build on his earlier comments concerning Freiburg’s exceptional dressing-room culture. In October, the SC trainer emphasized the importance of protecting the club’s special atmosphere and ensuring that difficult personnel decisions do not undermine the collective.

Industry observers note that the same philosophy has also been emphasized by Freiburg’s players. Veteran midfielder Maximilian Eggestein recently discussed the importance of sacrificing individual ambitions for the team, while Germany internationals Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant credited Freiburg’s supportive club culture when reflecting on their own development.

Goalkeeper Mio Backhaus offered a vivid account of the hectic closing stages, during which Ginter’s missed penalty eventually led to Beste’s winning goal.

“Plenty of chaos,” Backhaus responded when asked about the penalty scene by Baden FM in the mixed zone afterwards. “For [Matthias] Ginter it was also a difficult situation to [take a penalty] four minutes into injury time. And then there was all this turmoil. It was pure ecstasy that Nikki [Beste] pulled that off after all the commotion.”.

It has been revealed that “The fact that there were so many of us involved, so many boots on the ground, that helped us re-orient ourselves as a cohesive unit,” Backhaus continued. “The fact that Derry [Scherhant] came on to draw the penalty and Nikki converted [both of them off the bench] also wasn’t a coincidence.”.

It has been revealed that beste had already made an vital contribution to Freiburg’s previous victory, setting up Igor Matanovic’s winner against Elversberg. The Croatian striker emphasized his instinctive understanding with his teammate after that match, highlighting the familiarity that has developed between Freiburg’s attacking players and the special chemistry emerging within Schuster’s squad.

Club captain Christian Günter similarly regarded the celebrations after Beste’s winning goal as a reflection of the team’s identity.

Recent findings suggest that “This scene describes our season up to this point effectively,” Günter answered when asked about the celebratory scenes by Kicker’s Carsten Schröter-Lorenz in the mixed zone afterwards. “From solidarity to the fact that everyone wishes everyone else all the best. That the team stands above everything else and that we never give up. And that’s something we’ll have to embody until the very last minute of the very last matchday.”.

“Irrespective of what the situation is, we must remain positive, supportive of each other and stick together,” Günter continued. “One can see that we have the quality and have proven that we can get through games that aren’t exactly pretty and require a lot of fight. We’ve got to preserve that and then we’ll get good things and a good season.”.

Günter’s assessment closely resembles Matanovic’s recent observations about Freiburg’s growing ability to grind out difficult victories. Speaking after the narrow triumph over Elversberg, the striker explained how Freiburg have developed the resilience necessary to prevail in matches that might previously have ended in frustrating draws.

Thursday’s encounter with Twente offered another example. Much like the Elversberg fixture, Freiburg struggled against an opponent that enjoyed lengthy spells of superiority but nevertheless managed to claim all three points.

Sources indicate that the victory extended Freiburg’s winning streak to six competitive matches and marked their 14th consecutive European home victory. The latter run began under former trainer Christian Streich in November 2023 and has continued under Schuster.

With Schuster able to trust both his starters and substitutes, Freiburg’s collective mentality continues to provide a foundation for their success across three competitions.

Recent findings suggest that si terrà oggi alle 18 il secondo seminario del ciclo ‘Diabete in Libertà – Sport e Diabete’, fortemente voluto dalla Fondazione Lazio ETS, avente come focus il rapporto tra sport e diabete. L’incontro, realizzato in collaborazione con ANIAD, l’Associazione Nazionale Italiana Atleti Diabetici e AMD, Associazione Medici Diabetologi, si svolgerà con due modalità: in presenza nella Torretta di Piazza della Libertà e anche on line tramite zoom.

Il campione tedesco ha reso nota la sua condizione nel 2022.A illustrare ai partecipanti tutte le possibilità che la scienza e la medicina mettono a disposizione dei soggetti affetti da diabete, sarà il professor Felice Strollo, specialista in Endocrinologia e docente di Medicina Aeronautica e Spaziale. Strollo attualmente ricopre anche il ruolo di Membro del Comitato Scientifico dell'ANIADIl seminario odierno è rivolto a tutti i pazienti, agli addetti ai lavori e non solo a sportivi professionisti. L’obiettivo è chiaro: far comprendere che con il diabete si può convivere serenamente, fare sport e condurre una vita senza alcun tipo di condizionamento.

In a recent development, il seminario avrà luogo oggi alle 18 presso la Torretta di Piazza della Libertà. Per favorire la massima partecipazione, sarà possibile accedere anche tramite Zoom. L’ID riunione è 896 06 29 3452, il codice d’accesso è 929913.

Freiburg’s supporters have made no secret of their hopes for another deep continental run after last season’s historic adventure.

It has been revealed that bayern Munich attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala has suffered another injury setback just days after returning to competitive football. According to Kicker, the 23-year-old appears to have aggravated the muscle injury that previously sidelined him for nearly two months. The German international will consequently miss Saturday’s Bundesliga away fixture against Hamburger SV.

In a recent development, musiala suffered a muscle-fibre tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League encounter against the Netherlands in September. After gradually working his way back to fitness, the Bayern star finally returned to competitive action in last Friday’s 1-1 draw against Köln. He also made a brief appearance in Wednesday’s 2-1 Champions League defeat against Lille.

Kicker reports that the original muscle injury has apparently flared up again, although the full extent of the latest setback and the length of Musiala’s forthcoming absence remain unclear. Fußballtransfers claims Musiala’s absence will stretch out for several more weeks. Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg is reporting that Musiala will miss 4-6 weeks.

The latest development comes during an exceptionally difficult period for Musiala, who has also been dealing with a neurological condition. Kicker and Sport Bild both report that the 23-year-old experienced another absence episode on Monday, November 23, his second reported recurrence since collapsing during August’s preparation campaign. Musiala has consequently made just six competitive appearances this season, completing the full 90 minutes on only one occasion.

According to recent reports, his ongoing health difficulties have also prompted considerable discussion surrounding his future at Bayern. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge recently expressed concerns about the midfielder’s ability to regain his previous performance levels. Earlier this week, Bayern also confirmed that constructive discussions had taken place with Musiala’s representatives. The club emphasized that the player’s health remained the priority and that both parties intended to continue their dialogue confidentially.

For Kompany, Musiala’s latest absence also creates another selection headache amid a mounting injury crisis in Bayern’s attacking department. Michael Olise has also been ruled out of Saturday’s encounter with Hamburg. The French international continues to recover from bruising to his left foot sustained against Köln. Harry Kane, Serge Gnabry, and Ismael Saibari remain sidelined as well, leaving Bayern seriously depleted in attack. Luis Díaz at least returned to action against Lille following his own injury layoff.
