Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

📅 31 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5419 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.
  • There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be notable, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.
  • Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be notable, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

It has been revealed that “We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”.

In a recent development, asked if he at the moment has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really massive when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”.

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for new signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb.

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

Eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL.

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

It has been revealed that the goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

Sources indicate that one of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his fresh club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

Recent findings suggest that we lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

Recent findings suggest that to lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

Recent findings suggest that I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every significant team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

According to recent reports, every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

Industry observers note that [Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

It has been revealed that it was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

According to recent reports, I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ.

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who showed some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

John McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

In a recent development, arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Sources indicate that suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

Recent findings suggest that that was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

In a recent development, maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

In a recent development, garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

McGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

Garnacho → BarkleyWan-Bissaka → Cash.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

Sources indicate that suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Abraham → JacksonAlysson → Hemmings.

Bruno → OdegaardMerino → Lewis-Skelly.

Recent findings suggest that now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

In a recent development, gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

In a recent development, "It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL.

In a recent development, rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

It has been revealed that maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

In a recent development, eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Eze replaces Tzolis for Arsenal.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

According to recent reports, signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Industry observers note that only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Recent findings suggest that villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Sources indicate that calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

It has been revealed that gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the newly introduced signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

It has been revealed that tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

Industry observers note that suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

We’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

In a recent development, arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

Cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

According to recent reports, maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

Saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

According to recent reports, arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

According to recent reports, arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

According to recent reports, timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

According to recent reports, villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

Per l’ex compagno, i due tecnici hanno idee chiare; la Lazio attacca con molti uomini, mentre il Toro cerca stabilità.

Massimo Ambrosini presenta Torino-Lazio come la prima sfida in panchina tra i suoi ex compagni Ignazio Abate e Rino Gattuso. Secondo quanto riportato da La Stampa, La partita del 28 novembre 2026, allo stadio Grande Torino, mette di fronte i granata in cerca di rivincita e i biancocelesti, primi in classifica e ancora imbattuti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Ripensando al Milan dello scudetto 2010/11, Ambrosini racconta che si aspettava di vedere Gattuso allenatore, mentre Abate lo aveva sorpreso per la curiosità e l’applicazione mostrate nello studio del gioco: «Ero quasi sicuro che Rino sarebbe diventato un allenatore, Ignazio un po’ meno. È sempre stato un grande entusiasta e una persona positiva, ma non lo facevo così curioso e applicato dal punto di vista teorico». Di quella squadra sono diventati tecnici anche Nesta, Inzaghi, Seedorf, Oddo e Pirlo.

Industry observers note that commentatore di Dazn, che trasmetterà l’incontro, Ambrosini si aspetta una prova coraggiosa dal Torino. Giocando in casa, i granata possono cercare una svolta senza lasciarsi intimidire dalla capolista. La Lazio, invece, dovrebbe continuare ad attaccare con molti uomini, senza modificare la propria idea di gioco in base all’avversario.

«Il Toro deve fare una partita coraggiosa perché gioca in casa e può dare una svolta, quindi mi aspetto una prova gagliarda da parte di una squadra che non si spaventerà di affrontare la capolista. La Lazio, invece, giocherà come sempre: vorrà fare la partita, attaccando con tanti uomini. Rino ha già fatto vedere che cambiano gli avversari, ma non la sua idea di calcio», dice Ambrosini.

According to recent reports, quanto a una possibile carriera personale in panchina, la risposta dell’ex centrocampista è netta e scherzosa: «No, non mi avranno mai (ride, ndr). Sto bene così».

According to recent reports, per Ambrosini, il primato della Lazio si lega alle capacità di Gattuso e al lavoro svolto su una base già solida. L’ex capitano rossonero ricorda il calcio espresso dalle squadre allenate da Rino al Milan e al Napoli, distinguendo da quelle esperienze la parentesi in Nazionale, che considera particolare anche per i giocatori a disposizione.

«Rino lo conosco bene e conosco la capacità che ha di far giocare le proprie squadre. Al di là della Nazionale, una parentesi molto particolare anche per gli uomini che aveva a disposizione, Milan e Napoli giocavano un bel calcio con lui. È la sua storia che lo racconta e se la gente ha la memoria corta... Poi da lì a pensare che una squadra nella situazione in cui era la Lazio, con tutto quello che gli gira intorno, potesse fare questo tipo di percorso... Non se lo aspettava neanche lui, ma è giusto che sia primo per quel che sta facendo in campo», osserva Ambrosini.

Alla base del rendimento biancoceleste indica l’empatia costruita dal tecnico e i principi di gioco: «C’era una base solida, ma l’empatia creata da Gattuso e i principi di gioco hanno fatto la differenza». Il lavoro sulla fiducia, secondo Ambrosini, ha inciso anche sulla crescita dei singoli.

In a recent development, «La testa è fondamentale, ma non basta. Gattuso ha saputo tirare fuori il meglio da Isaksen, Frattesi o Taylor perché ha dato le conoscenze giuste per farli sentire in fiducia: così riesci a sfruttare il potenziale tecnico e atletico di ognuno», spiega.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.

Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.

Instead, Man United saw their numbers reduced inside the opening stages of the game after a reckless challenge by Leny Yoro, and 2-0 down after 13 minutes, with the club legend resorting to drastic methods to convey the side's weaknesses.

Of his old club's defenders, he remarked: 'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

Gary Neville took to slapping himself to convey the lack of focus he sees in Man United's stars.

The club legend had previously tipped his old side to have a stronger XI than Liverpool's.

But when the two teams met at Anfield, Man United were left woefully exposed after going down to 10 men.

The Overlap broadcaster then slapped his own face a number of times repeating 'wake up!' before adding: 'You play for Man United'.

The gesture left Carragher in stitches, with the Anfield icon collapsing onto the sofa in hysterics - although less impressed with Roy Keane, who displayed his usual sangfroid.

So tickled by the moment was the former Liverpool star that he later changed his profile picture on social media site X to a still image of Neville's hand catching his face.

Neville had more sharp criticism for Man United's defensive selection assessing the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in the starting line-up.

The Dutch defender has been out of Premier League action for 51 weeks after suffering a back injury, but was named by Mauricio Pochettino in his first-ever XI.

In a recent development, 'I have a lot of sympathy for him,' Neville admitted. 'It's like playing football after having six pints. It's a strange feeling.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him, it's alarming to watch.'.

Less sympathy for Man United's players came from Keane, who attacked the team - and Neville and Carragher - after the heavy defeat at Anfield confirmed the club's worst start in over 53 years.

The firebrand midfielder was on his usual caustic form as he assessed the damage, hitting out at those who might have accepted the score line, having feared a greater deficit.

Industry observers note that 'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

Industry observers note that 'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

According to recent reports, 'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

Recent findings suggest that 'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

The difference between the two teams felt a far cry from Neville's late-summer prediction, when he told Carragher that he had greater hopes for Carrick and Man United over incoming manager Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

'I think Manchester United are currently in a better place than Liverpool,' Neville noted in August. 'Would you agree?'.

Carragher said that he did not, and will have been confident in his assessment on Sunday night.

Pep Guardiola, allenatore, ha rilasciato un’intervista a Romario a Romario Tv: “È uno dei miei più grandi onori che hanno pensato a me per allenare la nazionale italiana, ma sentivo di dovermi fermare. Se me ne avevano parlato anni prima, probabilmente avrei accettato, ma all’epoca, con Paolo Maldini e Leonardo, mi sono reso conto che dovevo fermarmi. Avevo bisogno di più tempo per me stesso. Sono stato allenatore per 18 anni, allenando ogni tre giorni. È la prima volta che ne parlo, ma mi vergognavo di aver detto di no a un Paese come l’Italia. In nazionale il tempo è limitato. Ancelotti? Lui si adatta a questi tempi più ristretti. Ma non potrei mai dubitare delle capacità di Carlo. È impossibile, perché lo conosco. È un leader nella gestione del gruppo. Dicono che sia il numero uno. L’ho affrontato, è molto intuitivo, intelligente nelle sue decisioni tattiche. Poi sa anche lui che se non vinci non duri. Il Portogallo deve dargli l’addio che merita. Entrambe le parti devono impegnarsi affinché ci sia un finale degno della sua carriera. Cristiano non può lasciare la nazionale portoghese in questo modo, non possono permettere che Cristiano se ne vada in questo modo”.

Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.
  • The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the upcoming City head coach, has landed his number one target.
  • Recent findings suggest that city left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the upcoming City head coach, has landed his number one target.

Recent findings suggest that city left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Industry observers note that having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our upcoming Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855.

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

According to recent reports, “Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

Recent findings suggest that “I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

In a recent development, “But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve noted it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

Industry observers note that “But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”.

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw.

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club demonstrated an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Industry observers note that chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn.

The 21-year-old midfielder who came through the ranks at Real Madrid has been signed from Stuttgart.

Brighton’s sporting director Mike Cave noted: “We’re delighted to welcome Chema to the club. He has an excellent pedigree having come through at Real Madrid; he followed that with a very good season with Stuttgart last season.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”.

Fernandez indicates: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

Industry observers note that “If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join.

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Speaking about the Enzo Fernández deal on Sky Sports, Carragher said: “It pushes them above Chelsea. Myself and plenty of others felt Chelsea would have a really good season, and I still believe that.

“A lot of that is on the back of no European football, having a new manager and the front three they have got.

“But losing Enzo Fernandez, who for me over the last two or three years has been one of the big players for Chelsea... they’ve always had five or six top players but maybe not a lot around them.

“They’ve let one of them go, to Man City, it’s a huge fee but City look a lot stronger now and I’d say they are going to be the main challengers to Arsenal.”.

Chelsea had been holding off from sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City while they searched for a new midfielder of their own.

But City’s willingness to agree a £125m package has convinced Chelsea to give the green light to the Fernández move without any guarantees over an incoming signing.

Chelsea still have a few hours to try to make something happen, having had a bid for Lamine Camara turned down.

But Chelsea ultimately felt they had no choice but to let Fernández, who made it clear he wanted to leave, go in the best interests of the club.

Chelsea believe they have a strong squad, regardless of whether or not a new player is signed today, and will continue to weigh up their options.

The medicals are under way for Jack Grealish, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Folarin Balogun at Everton but there is no clarity on when all three deals will be concluded. Fulham are progressing quite quickly on three deals: Hugo Larsson (Frankfurt), Manuel Angel (Real Madrid) and David Affengruber (Elche).

Chelsea have agreed a £125m package to sell Enzo Fernández to Manchester City so the saga is finally coming to a close.

Chelsea will be happy with a fee that equals the British transfer record and City head coach Enzo Maresca will be delighted to land his top target.

It feels like a win-win all round as Fernández wanted to leave Chelsea and the club wanted over £120m after their initial deadline to do a deal expired.

It remains to be seen if Chelsea land any of their three main deadline day targets with a few hours of the window to go.

Chelsea had a bid rejected for Lamine Camara, Roma have not been playing ball on Manu Kone and the identity of the mystery Premier League target has not yet emerged.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”.

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”.

Sources indicate that “If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”.

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

Recent findings suggest that this has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Sources indicate that another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

It has been revealed that spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

According to recent reports, A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A substantial year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

It has been revealed that A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Sources indicate that barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

In a recent development, praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

Monza, Juric: "Dobbiamo andare oltre i nostri limiti per mettere in difficoltà la Roma"

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ivan Juric, tecnico del Monza, ha parlato in conferenza stampa in vista della sfida di domenica con la Roma.
  • Industry observers note that mister, dopo la vittoria sulla Fiorentina avrebbe preferito evitare una Roma in grande forma, allenata tra l'altro dal suo maestro e amico Gasperini?
  • "Non mi dispiace, perché prima o poi devi affrontare tutti.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ivan Juric, tecnico del Monza, ha parlato in conferenza stampa in vista della sfida di domenica con la Roma.

Industry observers note that mister, dopo la vittoria sulla Fiorentina avrebbe preferito evitare una Roma in grande forma, allenata tra l'altro dal suo maestro e amico Gasperini? Inoltre, molti suoi colleghi sostengono che seguire la partita dalla tribuna, quando si è squalificati, permetta di cogliere meglio alcuni aspetti tattici. È d'accordo?

"Non mi dispiace, perché prima o poi devi affrontare tutti. Non penso mai a evitare qualcuno: li affronti e basta. Per quanto riguarda la seconda domanda, è vero, spesso anche durante gli allenamenti ci mettiamo in alto per osservare meglio le situazioni. Dalla tribuna si vedono alcune cose in maniera più chiara, come è successo anche l'altro giorno, mentre altre si notano meno: i piccoli particolari, le espressioni dei giocatori, alcuni aspetti che dalla panchina riesci a cogliere meglio. A livello tattico, però, dall'alto si vede sicuramente di più. Ricordo, per esempio, una partita dell'Atalanta contro il Paris Saint-Germain, quando un allenatore aveva seguito il primo tempo dalla tribuna ed era poi sceso per apportare le modifiche necessarie.".

Tornando alla partita con la Fiorentina, cosa ha visto meglio dalla tribuna rispetto alla panchina? Dal punto di vista tattico, il centrocampo a cinque, anche con il rientro di capitan Pessina, è attualmente l'assetto che garantisce maggiore equilibrio e pericolosità?

In a recent development, "All'inizio la partita non mi era sembrata positiva, perché non eravamo aggressivi come avrei voluto. Dal 25' abbiamo iniziato a recuperare più palloni, a spingere e a prenderci qualche rischio in più. Abbiamo preso in mano la partita e, nei venti minuti finali del primo tempo e nei primi quindici della ripresa, abbiamo fatto quello che chiedevo: abbiamo segnato, creato un'altra occasione con Brindelli e una con Pessina, dominando la gara. Magari abbiamo concesso qualcosa in contropiede, ma era proprio quello che volevo vedere. Successivamente ci siamo abbassati per gestire il risultato.

In a recent development, per quanto riguarda l'assetto tattico, le richieste che faccio ad Akinsanmiro sono le stesse che facevo a Ngonge e Colpani. Cambia però l'interpretazione del ruolo: Akinsanmiro può darci qualcosa in più in determinate situazioni, nei raddoppi e nella compattezza. Devo dire, comunque, che anche Ngonge e Colpani hanno svolto un buon lavoro difensivo. In fase offensiva, invece, magari ci manca qualcosa rispetto alle loro caratteristiche. Akinsanmiro è molto bravo negli inserimenti, riesce a portare via altri giocatori e a liberare spazi per i compagni. È sicuramente un'opzione valida.".

Qual è l'aspetto che teme maggiormente della Roma? E secondo lei la squadra di Gasperini è una delle candidate allo scudetto?

Recent findings suggest that "Basta guardare i risultati: segnano quattro o cinque gol a partita. Ogni squadra che va all'Olimpico rischia davvero tanto, ma anche in trasferta stanno attraversando un momento straordinario. Hanno gioco e qualità. Gasperini è riuscito a trasmettere alla squadra tutto quello che aveva in mente e probabilmente continuerà a farlo. Adesso si vede che vanno forte: sono una squadra difficilissima da affrontare.

Per quanto riguarda lo scudetto, la considero una delle principali candidate insieme all'Inter. Vedremo se anche la Lazio riuscirà a mantenere questo ritmo, ma la Roma sta andando davvero forte. In questo momento mi sembra quella più difficile da affrontare, con più soluzioni offensive e un gioco che rende complicato capire da dove possa arrivare il pericolo.".

According to recent reports, poco più di un mese fa avete affrontato la Roma all'Olimpico, giocando molto bene soprattutto nel secondo tempo e mostrando grande coraggio anche in inferiorità numerica. Domenica potrebbero servirvi lo stesso atteggiamento e una maggiore attenzione?

It has been revealed that "Ho notato che le squadre che provano soltanto a chiudersi e a gestire gli spazi, senza aggredire la Roma, fanno molta fatica e finiscono per subire anche cinque gol. Chi invece prova ad aggredirla riesce a metterla in difficoltà, anche se deve riuscire a mantenere quell'intensità per tutta la partita. Finché ci riesce, può creare problemi alla Roma. Noi faremo la nostra partita, seguendo le nostre idee e cercando di andare oltre i nostri limiti per metterli in difficoltà.".

Recent findings suggest that domenica tornerà all'Olimpico da avversario della Roma, dopo la difficile esperienza sulla panchina giallorossa. Che accoglienza si aspetta? E da quell'esperienza si è portato via qualche insegnamento umano o professionale che oggi le torna utile a Monza?

"Penso che siano soprattutto le esperienze negative a insegnarti di più. Anche quelle che ho vissuto io sono state molto utili, anche se emotivamente non è stato facile affrontarle. Sono proprio le esperienze negative che ti fanno crescere maggiormente. Quelle belle ed entusiasmanti le ricordi con piacere, ma credo che dalle difficoltà si impari di più. In ogni caso, la vita va avanti: raccogli quello che hai imparato e guardi al futuro. Adesso c'è il Monza, il mio obiettivo è capire come deve giocare questa squadra e come far crescere i ragazzi. Ho soltanto questo in testa.".

In a recent development, nelle ultime partite abbiamo visto il passaggio a un centrocampo più solido, con cinque centrocampisti. La fase difensiva è nettamente migliorata?

"Per me no, assolutamente. Voi vi basate sui gol subiti, ma non considerate i tiri, le occasioni e quello che succede in campo. Non sono d'accordo. La partita contro l'Atalanta, per esempio, è stata imparagonabile rispetto a quella contro la Fiorentina: abbiamo fatto molto meglio contro l'Atalanta, anche se abbiamo perso. Nel primo tempo contro di loro abbiamo concesso zero occasioni. È diverso. Secondo me si guarda soltanto ed esclusivamente al risultato.".

In un certo senso possiamo dire che anche il Monza ha i suoi Dybala e Malen, in Varela e Robinson. Da qui a gennaio sarà importante recuperare e riabilitare, anche dal punto di vista mentale, giocatori che oggi sono diventati seconde linee, come Cutrone e Colpani?

Industry observers note that "Io aggiungerei anche Ngonge e Zeballos, oltre naturalmente a Cutrone e Colpani. Il calcio è fatto così: quando giochi una volta a settimana hai due ragazzi che stanno facendo davvero bene. In questo momento inserirei anche Motta, che ogni volta che entra mi dà grandi soddisfazioni per il modo in cui interpreta la partita, per l'entusiasmo e per quel sorriso che porta in campo.

According to recent reports, È chiaro quello che dici, ma anche l'altra sera, nella partita del Paris Saint-Germain, abbiamo visto un esempio clamoroso: al 60' sono entrati Dybala e Malen. Nel calcio di oggi, con questi ritmi e questa intensità, avere tanti giocatori di qualità diventa fondamentale. Spero davvero che questi ragazzi non si sentano sottovalutati, ma che continuino a lavorare forte e possano darci una grande mano durante le partite.".

It has been revealed that il clean sheet contro la Fiorentina ha dato morale al reparto difensivo. In particolare, Andrea Carboni ha disputato una grande prestazione. Come valuta la sua partita? Ci sono novità sugli infortunati e come mai Ciurria non è stato convocato nell'ultima gara?

It has been revealed that "Sono molto contento per Carboni, perché penso che abbia disputato una bellissima partita. Non so se sia stata la sua migliore prestazione, ma è stato sempre molto concentrato. È un ragazzo con una mentalità pazzesca. Ha riposato per due o tre settimane e anche questo, a volte, serve per recuperare energie. Ha fatto davvero una bella prestazione.

According to recent reports, per quanto riguarda Ciurria, in questo momento siamo in 27 e devo fare delle scelte, non soltanto per le partite ma anche durante gli allenamenti. È una situazione complicata: quando organizzi le partitelle dieci contro dieci, devi lasciare fuori quattro o cinque giocatori. Spero che questa situazione si risolva a gennaio, perché è dannosa e non mi piace per niente.

Purtroppo, dopo l'infortunio, Ciurria è rimasto fuori dalle rotazioni. È un momento particolare per lui e mi dispiace. Per quanto riguarda gli infortuni, Akinsanmiro ha preso una brutta botta all'inizio e ha avuto bisogno anche di alcuni punti di sutura. Ieri non è riuscito ad allenarsi, oggi ha fatto qualcosa e spero di averlo a disposizione. Per il resto, dalla prossima settimana dovrebbero esserci tutti.".

Sources indicate that il recupero di Ziolkowski permetterà alla difesa di fare un ulteriore salto di qualità? Come procede invece la competizione tra i due portieri, Tornqvist e Thiam?

It has been revealed that "Ziolkowski è un giocatore di grandissimo potenziale e ha ampi margini di miglioramento sotto diversi aspetti, come del resto tutti i nostri giocatori, a eccezione di qualche elemento più esperto. È già diventato un giocatore che può scendere in campo, entrare e darci una mano. Siamo contenti di lui e ha le caratteristiche giuste per essere importante per la squadra.

According to recent reports, per quanto riguarda Thiam e Tornqvist, come per tutti i nostri giocatori, vedo aspetti positivi e altri negativi. Per giocare devono essere al cento per cento, sia mentalmente sia fisicamente. Penso che Thiam abbia fatto due settimane ottime. Quando è rimasto qui avevo bisogno di un portiere bravo nelle uscite in determinate situazioni, perché immaginavo che nel finale potessero arrivare diversi cross verso Pellegrino e Beto. Ha lavorato molto bene e ci ha dato anche la possibilità di ripartire.

According to recent reports, per il momento non ho stabilito una gerarchia precisa: a volte giocherà uno, a volte l'altro. Abbiamo cambiato anche il modo di difendere sui calci piazzati, passando alla marcatura a uomo, che non avevo mai utilizzato prima. Finora è andata bene. Proviamo soluzioni e varianti diverse perché voglio che tutti siano motivati e concentrati, senza sapere in anticipo quello che succederà.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino suggested the Leny Yoro red card that had such an affect ontheir defeat by Liverpool game was 'unfair' and that their opponents should have been 'punished' too.

Pochettino gave up his job as US national team coach to join United on Wednesday, but any hope of a latest manager 'bounce' evaporated after Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes and his team were thrashed 4-0.

It was the joint-heaviest defeat for a latest United manager since Lal Hilditch a century ago, and leaves Pochettino's side second from bottom of the Premier League.

It has been revealed that 'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine, who blamed the early red card for United's defeat. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

'It's clear that after eight minutes the strategy was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

Sources indicate that 'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino blamed Leny Yoro's red card for his side's defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro (right) was sent off for fouling Alexander Isak inside eight minutes of Sunday's game.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

It has been revealed that 'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

Recent findings suggest that 'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

Pochettino was unhappy that referee Sam Barrott showed Yoro a straight red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak, having taken no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty box moments earlier.

Sources indicate that 'In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it,' added the United boss. 'If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper.

Recent findings suggest that 'If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth.'.

He later added: 'One centre-back made a mistake and wasn't punished and us, we made one mistake and we were punished.'.

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes agreed their team-mate should not have been sent off.

United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with Pochettino that it wasn't a red card.

In a recent development, 'No chance,' stated Mainoo. 'The ball is already with the keeper, and they're both running full speed. What can he do?

'I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

In a recent development, 'It's hard but no-one is going to save us. We have to come together and keep digging, keep fighting, and it will come round.'.

Captain Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, added: 'I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card, and I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR with a long time to see, do it in slow motion, and make a mistake like this which can change the game.'.

Gary Neville, who was left slapping himself in the face in shock live on Sky Sports, was pleased with damage control on, with United conceding four when it looked at one point that it would have been many more.

Former United captain Roy Keane, however, wasn't, and took aim at his ex-side's display.

'I thought United were desperate,' he said. 'So bad. Neville's OK with 4-0? Are you telling me they could have done better? 4-0 is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done.

Roy Keane (pictured), meanwhile, questioned why Gary Neville was pleased with the scoreline.

Industry observers note that 'People who played for the club said 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish?

'Liverpool were excellent but how easy did United make it for them? This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

'Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

Tra i profili maggiormente apprezzati dalla dirigenza dei Red Devils figura quello di Maximiliano Araujo, osservato da vicino anche in occasione del confronto di Champions League di mercoledì scorso, terminato 2-2. L'uruguaiano ha disputato tutti i 90 minuti, fornendo anche l'assist per la rete del momentaneo vantaggio portoghese firmata da Luis Suarez.

Sources indicate that secondo quanto riportato da Sport Witness, il classe 2000 sarebbe particolarmente interessato alla prospettiva di trasferirsi a Old Trafford e il suo entourage sarebbe disponibile ad avviare una trattativa. Il Manchester United, che deve fare i conti con i frequenti problemi fisici di Luke Shaw, potrebbe intervenire sulla fascia sinistra già a gennaio. Sia Shaw che Harry Amass, peraltro, hanno un contratto in scadenza nel giugno del 2027.

In a recent development, araujo ha rinnovato lo scorso agosto il proprio contratto con lo Sporting fino al 2030, inserendo nell'accordo una clausola rescissoria da 80 milioni di euro. Secondo la medesima fonte, tuttavia, un'offerta compresa tra i 50 e i 60 milioni potrebbe essere sufficiente per convincere la società lusitana a privarsene già durante il mercato invernale. Resta da capire se la dirigenza del Manchester United sarà disposta ad autorizzare un investimento di tale portata a metà stagione per rinforzare la rosa a disposizione di Mauricio Pochettino.

"Con Varela ho una storia piuttosto curiosa, perché Gustavo Varela è il figlio di Fernando Varela, un difensore centrale che è stato un mio giocatore ai tempi del PAOK. Quando sono arrivato al PAOK, Fernando era addirittura uno dei capitani della squadra. In quel periodo aveva trovato poco spazio e alla fine ha deciso di tornare in Portogallo per concludere lì la propria carriera. E ha portato con sé anche suo figlio.

A dire la verità, non seguivo molto le partite dell'Under 17, ma mi parlavano già molto bene di lui. Mi dicevano che aveva un grande fiuto del gol, che aveva proprio il senso del gol. Tech Report: Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double
