📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

According to recent reports, on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

It has been revealed that so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Industry observers note that mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

In a recent development, there are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Recent findings suggest that for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A substantial European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola stated, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Industry observers note that liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo demonstrated he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

In a recent development, as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

Sources indicate that it owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

According to recent reports, we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

In a recent development, this is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

It has been revealed that szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

Industry observers note that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

It has been revealed that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

Recent findings suggest that the Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

Sources indicate that the Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

It has been revealed that the idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

In a recent development, A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Sources indicate that atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Industry observers note that liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Major test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Sources indicate that liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

Industry observers note that we are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed latest contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

It has been revealed that “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

According to recent reports, “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

Industry observers note that former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Industry observers note that when Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

Recent findings suggest that “This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what massive clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola mentioned. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Atletico Madrid presently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

It has been revealed that “We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone remarked. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

‘I was distraught’: Ex-Sheffield United player has say on ‘disappointing’ Bramall Lane exit

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that sheffield United cut ties with the striker following their last promotion to the Premier League.
  • Sharp, now 40, had three separate spells as a player at Bramall Lane.
  • He has opened up about his departure from his boyhood club three-and-a-half years ago on Sky Sports’ Essential EFL Podcast: “I had a chance about three or four years before (to leave), Colorado Rapids were potentially going to take me but it wasn’t the right time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sheffield United cut ties with the striker following their last promotion to the Premier League. SUFC decided not to hand him a contract extension at Bramall Lane and he subsequently became a free agent.

Sharp, now 40, had three separate spells as a player at Bramall Lane. He announced his retirement in October but has since featured in non-league for AFC Rushden & Diamonds.

He has opened up about his departure from his boyhood club three-and-a-half years ago on Sky Sports’ Essential EFL Podcast: “I had a chance about three or four years before (to leave), Colorado Rapids were potentially going to take me but it wasn’t the right time. I didn’t leave Sheffield United. Sheffield United didn’t offer me a latest contract which was so disappointing for me because I got told by the owners and by the manager three times that I was going to get another year. I got told on the day of the parade that I wasn’t going to get it which absolutely ruined the day for me.

“I was distraught. I was going to retire at 37, that was me thinking ‘do you know what, I’ve had such a good career and I can’t see myself playing for another team’. I wanted to end at Sheffield United but I was out of contract for the first time in my career and (then) LA Galaxy came calling.”.

In a recent development, sharp rose up through Sheffield United’s academy as a youngster and was a regular for them at various different youth levels. He went on to play twice for SUFC’s first-team before leaving for Scunthorpe United in 2005.

Sources indicate that the Blades re-signed him two years later and he scored 13 goals in 64 matches before embarking on spells at Doncaster Rovers, Southampton, Nottingham Forest, Reading and Leeds United. Chris Wilder lured him back to his hometown team for a third time when they were in League One in 2015.

Recent findings suggest that sharp helped Sheffield United rise from the third tier to the Premier League and found the net on 116 occasions in 311 outings. However, his former club didn’t offer him fresh terms under Paul Heckingbottom and he subsequently became available.

In a recent development, as he has now alluded to, he considered hanging up his boots before LA Galaxy came calling. His stint in America was brief though and he later returned with Hull City before Doncaster Rovers brought him back.

Recent findings suggest that sharp will go down as one of Sheffield United’s greatest ever strikers. He is a legend at SUFC and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see him go back there in some capacity down the line.

The Blades are currently looking to claw themselves out of the EFL and back into the top flight if possible. They drew 1-1 at home against Southampton on Tuesday night with midfielder Sydie Peck scoring a late equaliser.

Wilder‘s side are sat in 9th place in the table after 17 fixtures and they are only one place outside the play-offs. They are one point behind Swansea City in 8th and could rise into the top eight this weekend if results go their way.

Sheffield United face a tricky away trip down to QPR on Saturday. Their upcoming opponents are positioned in 7th.

Tech Report: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.
  • Sources indicate that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions.
  • According to recent reports, thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Sources indicate that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

According to recent reports, thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

According to recent reports, in five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

It has been revealed that “That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

According to recent reports, in the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

It has been revealed that there was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

According to recent reports, the Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

According to recent reports, to lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

According to recent reports, A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

According to recent reports, even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

It has been revealed that throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm.

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

"We missed so many significant chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH.

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Wed, October 21: Bayern Munich (A) 8pm.

Wed, November 4: Slavia Prague (A) 8pm.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm.

Wed, December 9: Real Madrid (H) 8pm.

Wed, January 20: Real Betis (A) 8pm.

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” remarked Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

Industry observers note that “He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

Recent findings suggest that couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:.

Possession: Napoli 42%-58% Arsenal.

Touches in opposition box: 9-52.

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

In a recent development, they kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Well that should have been that!

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

In a recent development, martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

According to recent reports, there will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

No chance for Milinković-Savić.

Industry observers note that there is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

“Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

“We have to turn over a upcoming leaf. We face a different challenge tomorrow. We’ll need to put in a technically excellent performance and be able to defend better than we did against Como and Inter.”.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

In a recent development, “It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”.

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:.

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:.

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano.

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola.

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your official Champions League MD1 Gunners 👊.

It has been revealed that good evening from a very sticky and humid Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where the temperature is just a little too high to be pleasant. Perhaps that will change in time for kick-off. Perhaps it’s not relevant if I feel a bit uncomfortable in my jeans. Readers can make their own minds up on that….

Anyway, this should be a fun game. The atmosphere is usually pretty intense in this part of the world and they will be up for this one. The absence of Scott McTominay due to a minor heart problem is good news for Arsenal, who are likely to make a few changes to the team that beat Chelsea so impressively at the weekend.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a fresh attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under latest manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they presently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

Despite the carnage at UK airports this week, Sam Dean has made it to Naples and will be bringing us updates from the continent.

  • In a recent development, romero, 26, is under contract at Sevilla until June 2028 meaning he still has just under two years left to run down on his deal in Spain.
  • Industry observers note that in this latest update regarding his situation this winter, Ficherio claim he has emerged on the radar of the Blues as they eye a potentially ambitious swoop for his signature.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City are being linked with the La Liga forward ahead of the January transfer window. BCFC have the chance to freshen up their squad with some reinforcements this winter as they eye promotion from the Championship under the guidance of head coach Chris Davies.

In a recent development, romero, 26, is under contract at Sevilla until June 2028 meaning he still has just under two years left to run down on his deal in Spain. He has made 11 appearances in all competitions this season and has chipped in with three goals and two assists.

Industry observers note that in this latest update regarding his situation this winter, Ficherio claim he has emerged on the radar of the Blues as they eye a potentially ambitious swoop for his signature. The report suggests that talks have already begun with his representatives over a possible switch over to England.

Sources indicate that birmingham City are in the play-offs after 17 fixtures along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, QPR and Swansea City and they won 2-0 away at Burnley last time out. They are back in action this weekend at home against Bolton Wanderers.

Industry observers note that birmingham City’s Luis Vazquez is facing an uncertain future. BCFC only signed him four months ago but he has struggled to make an impact and is reportedly wanted by Racing Club.

Industry observers note that marvin Ducksch could also leave in January. Therefore, the Blues will need to bring in some competition for August Priske up top.

Sources indicate that romero was said to be on Sheffield United and Ipswich Town’s shortlist back in July last year. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put at Sevilla.

Birmingham City could see the Spaniard as someone to bolster their attacking department. As well as down the middle, he can also play on the left flank as well if needed.

Romero has enjoyed plenty of game time at Sevilla in the Spanish top flight over recent years and would be an eye-catching addition for Birmingham City if they managed to get him through the entrance door. He would inject more quality into BCFC’s options going forward.

It has been revealed that the Andalusia-born man rocked up at Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan back in 2019. He then broke into the first-team 2023 and has since been a regular.

Sources indicate that davies’ men will be full of confidence after their victory at Burnley. They will be eager for more of the same against Bolton Wanderers as they look to close the gap on Middlesbrough, Stoke City and Wolves.
